title: The Live Cover
premise: Ada Ashgrove, a deniable-operations fixer for the fictional Meridian Consulate, is contacted by a stranger named Ilya who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of performing. The debt he repays is a stolen dossier proving that the 'incident' that broke her sleep was not an accident but an orchestrated purge ordered from inside her own embassy, implicating her mentor, Director Voss. As three governments maneuver to bury the file and a methodical assassin called the Cartographer closes in, Ada must smuggle the truth across a contested border before the checkpoint shifts change at dawn. In the end, Ada chooses truth over loyalty: she burns her own cover to expose Voss publicly, survives the crossing by sacrificing the dossier's physical copy while its contents go live worldwide, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Lena Montrose is the pen name of a former foreign-service analyst who spent six years in postings she still cannot name. She writes thrillers about the people who clean up after history, and lives quietly under a name that is, at least, real.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Insomniac and hollowed out since the incident eight months ago, Ada works the margins of the Meridian Consulate's dirty errands. A stranger, Ilya, corners her in a night market and insists she saved his life in Sarajevo — a city she's never filed a report from. He leaves her a key and a warning. Emotional beat: unease; the past she thought she knew develops a crack.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The key opens a locker containing a partial dossier on the incident: names redacted, but the pattern of the explosion doesn't match any official account. Ada runs quiet verification through old contacts and realizes someone inside the Consulate falsified the record. Voss summons her with suspicious warmth. Emotional beat: dread curdling into suspicion as loyalty and evidence begin to war.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed). A meticulous killer who maps his targets' routines like terrain receives a contract: retrieve the dossier, erase the courier chain, leave no geography behind. He begins charting Ada's life — her café, her dead drop, her insomnia. Emotional beat: cold menace; the reader sees the trap assembling before Ada does.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada probes her mentor, who deflects with charm and a promotion offer designed to buy silence. A second contact from the locker list turns up dead, staged as suicide, and Ada recognizes the staging style from her own training manual. She realizes the purge was internal. Emotional beat: betrayal; the father figure becomes the prime suspect.

chapters.title: Ilya's Version
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Flashback-threaded chapter revealing the truth of Sarajevo: Ada, wiped or misfiled, did extract him during a joint op that Voss used as cover for the incident. Ilya has spent years tracking the paper trail. He and Ada form an uneasy alliance built on a debt neither can fully verify. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two people made of aliases.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The dossier surfaces on rival radars: a domestic intelligence service wants it buried, a foreign ministry wants it weaponized, and the Consulate wants it gone. Ada plays them against each other to buy time, burning favors and identities. The Cartographer closes within one move. Emotional beat: escalating pressure; every ally is also a liability.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Safehouse betrayed, Ada and Ilya run a nightlong chase through rail yards and flooded tunnels. Ilya takes a bullet covering her escape with the only copy of the dossier. Cornered, Ada makes a copy of everything onto an untraceable drive and mails a dead-man's switch to a journalist. Emotional beat: grief and resolve; the cost of truth gets a face.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dual POV — Ada and the Cartographer. Dawn approaches; the border checkpoint rotates guards in ninety minutes, and the new shift includes Consulate assets. The Cartographer intercepts Ada at the crossing, and instead of fighting, offers her Voss's real bargain: her old life back, sleep included, for the drive. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive — the chance to be unbroken again.

chapters.title: The Live Cover
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV. At the checkpoint, Ada refuses the bargain and goes live: she streams the dossier's contents publicly, making herself and the truth too visible to kill quietly. The Cartographer, contract voided by exposure, stands down — and reveals Voss ordered the incident to protect a larger client. Voss is arrested mid-betrayal of his own government. Emotional beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed at maximum price.

chapters.title: What Sleeps Through the Night
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ada's POV. Weeks later, Ada testifies under her real name — the first one she's used in a decade — while the Consulate is quietly dissolved. Ilya recovers; they part without promises but with honesty. In a small apartment with no aliases attached, Ada sleeps until morning. Final beat: peace earned, not granted; loyalty to truth outlasted loyalty to power.
